panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 7 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G). A: Anterior full-body clinical photograph of the patient with acquired generalized lipodystrophy showing generalized fat loss, facial lipoatrophy and prominent musculature; eyes redacted. B: Right lateral clinical photograph showing generalized subcutaneous fat depletion with prominent musculature in the same patient. C: Posterior full-body clinical photograph demonstrating generalized fat loss with prominent musculature. D: Posterior view of left upper extremity showing subcutaneous fat loss and muscular prominence. E: Anterior view of left upper extremity with fat loss, muscular prominence and a hyperpigmented macule on the hand dorsum. F: Posterior trunk photograph showing gluteal fat loss with prominent musculature. G: Anterior view of calves and feet showing subcutaneous fat loss and increased skin pigmentation; pigmentation not explicitly diagnostic of acanthosis nigricans so captured as a proposed finding.
panels.attribution_text: Hoff et al. A Novel Subtype of Acquired Generalized Lipodystrophy Associated With Subcutaneous Panniculitis-Like T-cell Lymphoma.. JCEM case reports 2024. doi:10.1210/jcemcr/luae069. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Clinical features of the 52-year-old African American man with acquired generalized lipodystrophy due to subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma. A, Anterior; B, Right lateral; and C, Posterior view of the patient, showing temporal recession of hair, marked loss of fat from the temporal region and cheeks, from the neck, thorax, abdomen, upper extremities, thighs, and calves resulting in prominent musculature. There is focal loss of hair on the right temporal region and his eyebrows. D, Posterior; and E, Anterior view of the left upper extremity, showing loss of subcutaneous fat resulting in prominence of muscles. There was a hyperpigmented macular lesion of about 3 cm diameter on the dorsum of the left hand. F, Posterior view of the trunk showing prominent gluteal muscles due to loss of subcutaneous fat. G, Anterior view of the calf and feet showing increased pigmentation of the skin and loss of subcutaneous fat from the dorsum of the feet.

plate_findings.evidence: Caption: "Buccal fat pad loss with the prominent zygomatic arch"

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Frontal clinical photograph of the patient showing buccal fat pad loss with a prominent zygomatic arch, a facial manifestation of acquired generalized lipodystrophy documented in the article on ICI-induced AGL. Eyes are obscured with a black bar (annotation), but the facial findings remain clearly visible. B: Profile view of the same patient demonstrating buccal fat pad loss and a prominent zygomatic arch, consistent with the facial lipoatrophy of acquired generalized lipodystrophy described in the article caption.

findings.label: Acanthosis nigricans
findings.evidence: caption: 'Note the acanthosis nigricans on the axilla and pseudothelarche'

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of the axilla and breast; caption explicitly identifies acanthosis nigricans on the axilla plus pseudothelarche in a child with AGL confirmed by the article title. Acanthosis nigricans is a recognized cutaneous manifestation of AGL; pseudothelarche noted as an additional finding outside the vocabulary.
panels.attribution_text: Eren et al. Acquired generalized lipodystrophy associated with autoimmune hepatitis and low serum C4 level.. Journal of clinical research in pediatric endocrinology 2010. doi:10.4274/jcrpe.v2i1.39. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Note the acanthosis nigricans on the axilla and pseudothelarche
in_text_mentions: Her tonsils were hypertrophic. Remarkable acanthosis nigricans was present over the neck, axilla, and umbilicus (Figure 2). The abdomen was protuberant and distended with hepatosplenomegaly. The liver was palpable 6 cm below the costal margin and the spleen was massively enlarged, extending to the inguinal area. Dyspnea with subcostal retractions was present and coarse crackles were audible over the entire chest. There was a systolic murmur of 2-3/6 magnitude over the mesocardiac area. Her pubertal status was Tanner stage III for thelarche (pseudothelarche) and stage I for pubarche (Figure 3).
